target.title: fix(crestodian): classify approval intent on the utility model tier (#102360)
target.body:
## Summary

`classifyCrestodianApprovalIntent` resolved the agent's flagship model to decide a single approve/decline/other label, instead of the configured `utilityModel`. It was the only member of the simple-completion family that omitted `useUtilityModel: true`, so every ambiguous approval reply in the interactive approval/config flow was billed at flagship pricing for a fixed ~8-token structured answer.

Fixes #102360.

## What Problem This Solves

When an approval reply cannot be resolved by the closed-list matcher, `classifyCrestodianApprovalText` returns `other` and the model path runs. That path prepared the model without the utility flag (`src/crestodian/approval-intent.ts:100`), so `resolveSimpleCompletionSelectionForAgent` fell through to the flagship primary model. The classifier is a pure ternary over one short user message, fixed to `APPROVAL_INTENT_MAX_TOKENS = 8` output tokens, fail-closed (`other` leaves the proposal pending), and non-binding — there is no quality reason to hold the flagship tier while its label-generator sibling (`conversation-label-generator.ts:63`) already runs the utility tier for an equivalently small bounded task.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adding `useUtilityModel: true` routes the classifier to the utility tier when one is configured. When none is configured, `resolveSimpleCompletionSelectionForAgent` falls through to the same primary model it uses today, so the change is **zero-behavior** for those users and a pure saving (~10x flagship-vs-utility per-call cost) for those who set a `utilityModel`.

## Changes

- `src/crestodian/approval-intent.ts`: pass `useUtilityModel: true` to `prepareSimpleCompletionModelForAgent`.
- `src/crestodian/approval-intent.test.ts`: added a regression test asserting the classifier prepares the model with `useUtilityModel: true`.

## User Impact

Users who configure a distinct `utilityModel` no longer pay flagship pricing for the bounded approve/decline/other classification in the Crestodian approval flow. Users without a `utilityModel` see byte-identical model selection.

## Evidence

### 1. Real setup transcript (standalone, not a test harness)

A standalone script drove the production model-tier selector `resolveSimpleCompletionSelectionForAgent` (the function `prepareSimpleCompletionModelForAgent` delegates to) with the exact params approval-intent passes today vs. the same params plus the utility flag, on identical config:

```
# utilityModel configured
configured primary model = anthropic/claude-opus-4-1
configured utility model = anthropic/claude-3-5-haiku-latest
approval-intent BEFORE (no useUtilityModel) -> anthropic/claude-opus-4-1
approval-intent AFTER  (useUtilityModel:true) -> anthropic/claude-3-5-haiku-latest
# no utilityModel configured (safety: zero-behavior)
BEFORE (no useUtilityModel) -> anthropic/claude-opus-4-1
AFTER  (useUtilityModel:true) -> anthropic/claude-opus-4-1
```

With a `utilityModel` configured, the classifier currently selects the flagship (opus); adding the one flag moves it to the utility tier (haiku). With no `utilityModel` configured, selection is identical before and after — a zero-behavior, pure-saving change.

### 2. Regression test

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
```

The new test `classifies on the utility model tier, not the flagship` fails on `origin/main` (the call omits the flag) and passes with this patch. `oxlint` on the changed files passes clean.
